notes.11: All options were chosen, with option C being the most common response. This suggests some misunderstanding of the term ‘exothermic’ and in the use of energy level diagrams.
notes.12: This question was very poorly answered. All three options were given in preference to the correct answer. Candidates should recall that combustion reactions are exothermic.
notes.13: Option A was a common incorrect response. Although the volume of acid may affect overall rate when the other reactant is in excess, it is not always correct that increasing the volume will increase the reaction’s rate.
notes.15: The colours of different metal compounds were not well recalled. Option A was a common incorrect response.
notes.19: Option A was chosen by candidates who performed less well overall. In preparations of salts, it is usual to add an excess of an insoluble oxide or carbonate to neutralise all the acid and to allow easy separation of the excess by filtration.
notes.20: This question on ion tests was not well answered. The distribution of responses suggest that most candidates were guessing.
notes.22: Candidates tended to confuse the reactivity trend of Groups I and VII in this question. The most common response was option D .
notes.33: Candidates are often able to complete balanced equations. This question appeared to be slightly more demanding than in the past and some candidates found it difficult. They were more likely to choose option A , ignoring either the oxygen in CO 2 or the H 2 O from the equation.
notes.39: This was the best answered question on the paper. Nearly all candidates identified the correct catalyst for fermentation.
